'''Yvette Kosmann-Schwarzbach''' (born 30 April 1941)<ref>Birth date from [http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n93108267.html Library of Congress] and [https://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb12436908f French National Library], retrieved 2019-10-13</ref> is a French [[mathematician]] and [[professor]].

== Education and career ==
Kosmann-Schwarzbach obtained her [[doctoral degree]] in 1970 at the [[University of Paris]] under supervision of [[André Lichnerowicz]] on a dissertation titled ''Dérivées de Lie des spineurs'' ([[Lie derivative]]s of [[spinor]]s).<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=128977}}</ref>

She worked at [[Lille University of Science and Technology]], and since 1993 at the [[École polytechnique]].

== Research ==
Kosmann-Schwarzbach is the author of over fifty articles on [[differential geometry]], [[algebra]] and [[mathematical physics]], of two books on [[Lie group]]s and on the [[Noether's theorem|Noether theorem]], as well as the co-editor of several books concerning the theory of [[integrable systems]]. The [[Kosmann lift]] in differential geometry is named after her.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Fatibene | first1=L. | last2=Ferraris | first2=M. | authorlink3=Mauro Francaviglia | last3=Francaviglia | first3=M. | last4=Godina | first4=M. | title=A geometric definition of Lie derivative for Spinor Fields | journal=Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Differential Geometry and Applications | date=28 August – 1 September 1995 | location=Brno, Czech Republic | editor-last1=Janyska | editor-first1=J. | editor-last2=Kolář | editor-first2=I. | editor-last3=Slovák | editor-first3=J. | publisher=Masaryk University | pages=549–558}}</ref><ref>Godina M. and Matteucci P. (2003), ''Reductive G-structures and Lie derivatives'', ''[[Journal of Geometry and Physics]]'', '''47''', pp. 66–86</ref>
